title: Distribution-Aware Exploration for Adaptive HNSW Search

statements.text: Let $ q =(q_1,…,q_d)$ be a query vector, and let $ V $ be a dataset of data vectors, each of dimensionality $d$, and $ V $ is i.i.d. across its dimensions. Then, the full distance list $FDL_ IP ( q , V )$ converges in distribution to a normal distribution as $d ∞$: $ N (μ_ IP , σ^2_ IP )$ with the mean $μ_ IP $ and the variance $σ^2_ IP $: $μ_ IP = Σ_ i=1 ^ d q_i E [v_i];\ σ^2_ IP = Σ_ i=1 ^ d q_i^2 Var (v_i)$.

Let $ V $ be a vector dataset of $n$ data vectors, each of dimensionality $d$. Let $ v =(v_1, …, v_d)$ be a random data vector of $d$ random variables, where each $v_i$ represents the distribution of the values within the $i$-th column of $ V $. If the random variables $(v_1, …, v_d)$ are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.), then we say the dataset $ V $ is i.i.d across its dimensions.

Given a HNSW index, a query vector $ q $, and a user-specified expected recall, the adaptive \ for $ q $ is defined as the minimum \ value such that the search result of $ q $ over the HNSW index achieves the expected recall.
Given a query vector $ q $ and a dataset $ V = ( v _1, …, v _n) $, the Full Distance List (FDL) of $ q $ with respect to $ V $ is $FDL( q , V ) = (dist( q , v _1), …, dist( q , v _n) )$.

proofs.text: Consider the inner product $ q · v = Σ_ i=1 ^d q_i v_i$. The query vector $ q $ is given during similarity search online, such that each $q_i$ is a constant at query time. Then, the inner product is a sum of i.i.d random variables, where each is given by $q_i v_i$. According to the Central Limit Theorem, the sum follows a normal distribution as $d$ becomes large. For the mean and variance, we have: $ E [Σ_ i=1 ^d q_i v_i] = Σ_ i=1 ^dq_i E [v_i]$, and $ Var (Σ_ i=1 ^d q_i v_i) = Σ_ i=1 ^d q^2_i Var ( v_i)$.

bound_sents: This adaptive probing continues until the target recall is achieved or a predefined upper bound on \ is reached.

For HNSW (HNSWlib) and HNSW (FAISS) , we execute the query workload multiple times, gradually increasing \ starting from \ = $k$ for Top-$k$ ANNS, until either the average recall reaches $0.99$ or \ reaches a upper bound of 5000, and we report the execution time and corresponding recall.

The offline computation of Ada- includes: (i) computing dataset-level statistics ( Stats ), (ii) sampling 200 data vectors and computing their ground truth ( Samp. ), and (iii) constructing the -estimation table ( EF-Est. ) with an expected recall of 0.95 and an \ upper bound of 5000.
